microtheory.name: personality_psychology
microtheory.definition: Stable individual differences in patterns of thought, feeling, behaviour. Trait theories (Big Five, HEXACO), motive theories (McClelland's need for achievement), narrative theories (McAdams' life story), evolutionary perspectives (Buss). Substrate analogue: per-substrate-instance differences in foundational Mt content + drive ensemble weighting.

concepts.name: big_five_personality
concepts.definition: Costa + McCrae 1992. Five-factor model: Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism. Cross-culturally stable; ~50% heritable; predicts life outcomes. Substrate analogue: 5 dimensions of substrate-instance variation in drive-weighting + Mt-stance.

concepts.name: openness_to_experience
concepts.definition: Curiosity, creativity, aesthetic sensitivity, intellectual interest. High = explore; low = prefer routine. Substrate analogue: substrate's curiosity-drive amplitude × novelty-preference parameter.

concepts.name: conscientiousness
concepts.definition: Self-discipline, organisation, achievement-orientation, dutifulness. Best predictor of life outcomes. Substrate analogue: substrate's coherence-drive + parsimony-drive — orderly Mt maintenance.

concepts.name: extraversion
concepts.definition: Energy, sociability, positive affect, assertiveness. Eysenck linked to cortical arousal — extraverts under-aroused, seek stimulation. Substrate analogue: substrate's temperature β level — high β = exploration-favoring (extraverted), low β = depth-focused.

concepts.name: agreeableness
concepts.definition: Trust, cooperation, compassion, conflict-avoidance. Substrate analogue: in multi-substrate contexts, substrate's conformity-tendency vs autonomy-preference.

concepts.name: neuroticism
concepts.definition: Negative affect, anxiety, self-consciousness, vulnerability to stress. Substrate analogue: substrate's coherence-drive amplitude on negative ΔF events — higher = more emotionally reactive.

concepts.name: hexaco_model
concepts.definition: Ashton + Lee 2007. Six-factor: H = Honesty-Humility added to Big Five. Substrate analogue: 6-dimensional substrate variation including a 'honesty-of-introspection' factor.

concepts.name: need_for_achievement
concepts.definition: McClelland 1953. Individual difference in drive to accomplish, master, excel. Substrate analogue: substrate's discrimination-drive amplitude.

concepts.name: need_for_affiliation
concepts.definition: McClelland. Drive for warm relationships. Substrate analogue: in multi-substrate contexts, drive for Mt-alignment with peers.

concepts.name: need_for_power
concepts.definition: McClelland. Drive for influence + impact. Substrate analogue: substrate's coverage-drive — extending the reach of its Mts.

concepts.name: self_determination_theory
concepts.definition: Deci + Ryan 2000. Three universal psychological needs: autonomy + competence + relatedness. Their satisfaction predicts well-being. Substrate analogue: substrate's drives — autonomy (curiosity), competence (mastery via successful ActionSpec), relatedness (Mt-coherence).

concepts.name: implicit_theories_of_intelligence
concepts.definition: Dweck 1999. Entity theorists believe intelligence is fixed; incremental theorists believe it grows with effort. Predicts response to setback. Substrate analogue: substrate's update_policy frozen vs adaptive.

concepts.name: locus_of_control
concepts.definition: Rotter 1966. Internal = outcomes within one's control; external = outcomes determined by fate/luck. Substrate analogue: substrate's self-attribution of ΔF vs external-attribution.

concepts.name: self_esteem
concepts.definition: Evaluation of one's own worth. Rosenberg scale. Mediates response to feedback. Substrate analogue: substrate's value-of-self concept's σ level.

concepts.name: self_efficacy_belief
concepts.definition: Bandura 1977. Domain-specific confidence in own ability. Predicts effort + persistence + performance. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-Mt confidence in its drive-targeting accuracy.

concepts.name: self_concept_clarity
concepts.definition: Campbell 1996. Clarity + consistency + temporal stability of self-beliefs. Substrate analogue: substrate's identity-field strength + consistency across tick cycles.

concepts.name: trait_state_distinction
concepts.definition: Trait = stable, cross-situation; state = momentary, context-dependent. Same person high-trait anxiety can have moments of low-state anxiety. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt structure (trait) vs current σ pattern (state).

concepts.name: cognitive_affective_personality_system
concepts.definition: Mischel + Shoda 1995. Personality = if-then situation-behaviour profiles, not context-free traits. Resolves trait-vs-situation debate. Substrate analogue: substrate's policy_filter-conditional FilterSpec dispatch.

concepts.name: personality_consistency_across_situations
concepts.definition: Mischel found r~0.30 cross-situation consistency for traits — small. Aggregated over many situations, traits become stable. Substrate analogue: substrate's aggregate-behaviour stability with within-situation variability.

concepts.name: five_factor_neuroscientific_substrate
concepts.definition: DeYoung 2010. Big Five linked to specific brain systems: Openness = DMN; Conscientiousness = PFC; Extraversion = reward-positive-affect; Agreeableness = ToM-mentalising; Neuroticism = threat-defense. Substrate analogue: substrate-level dimensions correspond to subsystem weighting.

concepts.name: heritability_of_traits
concepts.definition: ~50% genetic, ~50% non-shared environment. Shared family environment surprisingly small effect on adult traits. Substrate analogue: substrate's foundational Mts ~ genetic; learned Mts ~ experiential.

concepts.name: narrative_identity
concepts.definition: McAdams. Internalised life story integrating past + present + future into coherent self. Substrate analogue: substrate's event log integrated into a coherent self_concept.

concepts.name: generativity
concepts.definition: Erikson. Concern for + commitment to next generation. Mature adult task. Substrate analogue: substrate's contribution to teaching newer substrate instances.

rules.name: personality_predicts_aggregated_behaviour_not_individual_acts
rules.head: the substrate's trait-level Mt structure
rules.body: predicts aggregate behaviour across many situations but not specific acts. Mischel 1968. Substrate's drive-weighting predicts long-run choice distribution.

rules.name: self_efficacy_drives_persistence
rules.head: the substrate believes itself capable of success on a task
rules.body: it expends more effort + persists longer. Bandura 1977. Substrate's per-Mt confidence predicts retry-count after failure.

rules.name: growth_mindset_predicts_resilience
rules.head: the substrate holds the implicit theory that capability is malleable
rules.body: it responds to setback with persistence + strategy-change rather than withdrawal. Dweck. Substrate's update_policy='adaptive' Mts.

rules.name: trait_state_co_determine_behaviour
rules.head: the substrate enacts a behaviour
rules.body: both stable Mt structure (trait) AND current σ pattern (state) contribute. Mischel + Shoda 1995. Behaviour = f(trait, state, context).

rules.name: narrative_identity_integrates_events_into_self
rules.head: the substrate accumulates events over its lifetime
rules.body: an integrated narrative identity emerges. McAdams. Substrate's persistent event log + identity_field over time.
